⏺ Deployed.

  What's shipped

  Why your JAMU can lost its label: the auto-fetched inspo images contained
  OTHER competitor cans/bottles, and NB Pro blended those product designs into
  the JAMU can. Classic contamination.

  Two fixes:

  1. Inspo preview panel
  When you tick Match a proven style, a preview box opens under the toggle:
  - Auto-fetches 4 real category ads
  - Shows them as thumbnails
  - × button on each to drop the ones that don't fit
  - ↻ Regenerate button to pull a fresh set
  - Only the images that survive get sent to NB Pro on shoot

  So next time you'll see the 4 competitor cans BEFORE spending credits — remove
   any that look like they'd contaminate your product, or regenerate for a
  cleaner set.

  2. Stronger "don't copy" hint
  The reference hint sent to NB Pro is now explicit:

  ▎ "These images CONTAIN OTHER PRODUCTS. IGNORE their specific products, 
  ▎ packaging, labels, colours, logos, and people. Only absorb lighting 
  ▎ direction, composition energy, camera angle, negative-space use, typography 
  ▎ treatment. Under no circumstances substitute or blend the hero product's 
  ▎ design with any product visible in these inspiration images."

  Try one more shoot of the JAMU can — with the preview panel you can pick 4
  inspo images that don't contain drink cans (splash shots, landscape ads,
  editorial hero shots) and see if the JAMU label survives cleanly.

⏺ Read it. This is a genuinely great production spec — very well thought out.
  Here's my read + questions before I build.

  What this format is

  A two-person podcast ad — 6 sequential Seedance 2.0 clips (5 dialogue + 1
  product-reveal outro), ~78s total, using two locked character references (host
   + expert) plus the product. Extremely detailed prompt scaffolding: pacing
  rules, skin realism, gesture logic tied to spoken words,
  audio-continues-under-cutaway cuts, locked studio setting.

  It maps well onto what you already have — influencers (with character sheets),
   product studio, Seedance pipeline. The novelty is: multi-shot narrative with 
  alternating dialogue + a product-reveal outro.

  What I'd build (in principle)

  A new format podcast-ad that:

  1. Adds a page /generate/podcast-ad: pick 2 actors (host + expert), pick 1
  product, pick length, enter a brief.
  2. Sonnet writes a full 6-shot script (or 3-shot short version) with proper
  dialogue, cadence notes, and per-shot cut sequences.
  3. Fires 6 Seedance jobs in sequence — shot 6 uses shot 5's last frame as the
  start frame + product image as an additional reference.
  4. Stitches into one final video via Shotstack (you already have this
  pipeline).
  5. Registers podcast-ad in the Campaign Planner format registry so it shows up
   in campaigns and the Format Library.

  Questions before I start

  1. Length / shot count. The reference is 6 shots / ~78s. Do you want:
  - Fixed 6-shot ~80s format (matches the guide, simpler to build)
  - User picks: 30s / 60s / 90s (I'd generate the shot list to match)
  - Just 3-shot short for TikTok / Reels tempo

  2. Dialogue authorship. Who writes what the characters say?
  - AI writes fully (Sonnet drafts based on brand + product + brief — user can
  edit)
  - User writes verbatim (user types the script, we split it into shots)
  - Hybrid (AI drafts, user edits before generation)

  3. Studio setting flexibility. The guide locks a white-boucle-studio look. Do
  you want:
  - Always this same studio (the "podcast look" is baked in and consistent —
  most reliable)
  - Preset options: sleek studio / cozy living room / dark cinematic / outdoor
  patio
  - Scene Studio integration — user picks any of their saved scenes

  4. Final product-reveal outro (shot 6). Always? Optional? For a mid-funnel
  "podcast clip" without a hard CTA, someone might want the 5 dialogue shots
  stitched without the pull-back-to-product ending.

  5. Where does it live?
  - Standalone page /generate/podcast-ad (dedicated builder)
  - Just a new format inside Campaign Planner (users plan podcast ads as one
  shot among many)
  - Both (standalone builder + registry entry so it's also planable)

  6. Cost. Each Seedance 1080p clip = ~330 cr × 6 shots ≈ ~2000 credits per 
  podcast ad (~$48 to your users). That's high. Do we:
  - Just show the price prominently and let them decide
  - Offer a "720p preview first" mode for ~half price so they can iterate
  cheaply, then re-render at 1080p
  - Force 720p only until user says "polish this to 1080p"

  7. Character requirement. Podcast ads need TWO influencers with character
  sheets. If a user only has one, we could:
  - Block them and prompt "create a second influencer first"
  - Auto-generate a co-star influencer in the flow (Sonnet + NB Pro creates a
  matching co-host from a short description)

  My defaults if you say "you decide":
  1. User picks 30s / 60s / 90s
  2. AI drafts, user edits before generation
  3. Always the same podcast studio (with future option to add presets)
  4. Product outro optional (toggle)
  5. Both — standalone page + Campaign Planner registry entry
  6. Show price + offer 720p preview mode
  7. Auto-generate co-star from a short description if only one influencer
  exists

  Answer the ones you care about (or say "your defaults") and I'll spec + build.

⏺ Removed and deployed. Now — Pinterest, honest read.

  Pinterest API reality check

  Their API doesn't offer public search of anyone's pins without heavy review.
  Basic API access only gives you:

  - CRUD on your own account's pins/boards
  - Analytics on your own account
  - Ads / campaigns (business review)

  The /v5/search/pins endpoint (which is what we'd need to fetch category inspo)
   requires either:
  1. Trusted partner status — weeks of Pinterest review, often denied for
  AI-generation use cases
  2. User-scoped OAuth with the user's own board — user creates a board,
  connects, we read their board

  Path 2 is realistic and immediate. Path 1 could work but you'll wait.

  What to tell the form

  For the fields in your screenshot:

  Objectif du développeur: → Autre (Other). MCP/AI connector might trigger extra
   review scrutiny. "Autre" is cleanest — write in the description something
  like:

  ▎ "AI content generation platform for DTC brands. Users connect their 
  ▎ Pinterest account to import their own curated inspiration boards into our 
  ▎ creative pipeline."

  Objectif de l'application: →

  ▎ "ContentFlow lets brands generate ad photos and videos with AI. This 
  ▎ integration lets a brand's user pull pins from their own Pinterest 
  ▎ inspiration boards as reference material for AI image generation. No public 
  ▎ search or scraping. Only OAuth-scoped access to boards the user has created 
  ▎ and connected."

  Cas d'utilisation: → tick "Applications pour utilisateur de Pinterest"
  (Pinterest user apps). This is the least-scrutinized category for OAuth-scoped
   read use cases.

  Lien vers la politique de confidentialité: → your contentflow-web.com/privacy
  URL (create the page if it doesn't exist — just a basic one).

  What I recommend actually building

  "Import from Pinterest" instead of "Match a proven style":

  1. In Product Studio, user clicks "Import from Pinterest".
  2. First time: they OAuth into Pinterest (basic scopes: boards:read,
  pins:read).
  3. We list their boards. They pick one (e.g., their "JAMU ad ideas" board).
  4. We fetch the pins from that board (10-20 images).
  5. Show as a preview panel — same UX as before, but the images are ones they 
  curated themselves = no contamination risk.
  6. Selected ones get passed to NB Pro as style refs.

  Why this is better than the Tavily version:
  - User-curated = no random competitor drinks contaminating the JAMU can
  - No approval required from Pinterest beyond app registration
  - Ships in a session once you have Pinterest API creds

  Downside: requires user setup (create a Pinterest board first). Not one-click
  magic like the Tavily attempt was supposed to be. But actually usable.

  What I need from you

  1. Fill the Pinterest form as above.
  2. Once approved, send me the PINTEREST_APP_ID + PINTEREST_APP_SECRET.
  3. Say go and I'll wire OAuth + board picker + import into Product Studio.

  Or if you want a middle ground: I can build the UI shell (Import from
  Pinterest button, board picker, preview panel) with a mock backend right now,
  and swap in real Pinterest API calls when you get approved. Say which.

❯ cant we make a small window appear in our app, that shows pinterest website   
  and people can do the search                                                  

⏺ Short answer: no, we can't embed Pinterest inside a window in our app.
  Pinterest (like every major site) sets X-Frame-Options: DENY which blocks
  iframing — same reason you can't iframe Google/Instagram/Facebook. The browser
   refuses to render them inside another site for security.

  What DOES work

  Three realistic paths, ranked by how fast we ship:

  1. Open Pinterest in a new tab + paste back (ships today, no approval needed)

  - User clicks "Find inspo on Pinterest" in Product Studio
  - We open pinterest.com/search/pins?q={your product category} in a new browser
   tab
  - User browses normally, right-clicks the pins they like → Copy image address
  - Paste URLs into a text box in our app
  - Server fetches those URLs → same NB Pro flow as before

  Pros: works right now, no Pinterest API needed. User picks exactly what they
  want.
  Cons: extra clicks (copy → paste), and Pinterest image URLs sometimes expire /
   block hotlinking.

  2. Upload your own inspo images (ships in 10 minutes, best UX)

  Skip Pinterest entirely — let the user drop 2–6 images they've already saved
  (from Pinterest, Instagram, screenshots, wherever). We already support one
  style reference upload; just extend it to multiple.

  This is what people actually do in real workflows anyway. They collect inspo,
  they know what they want.

  Pros: full control, no scraping fragility, no API dance, ships in minutes.
  Cons: not "magical AI fetches for you."

  3. Pinterest OAuth board import (when your API app is approved)

  The path I described earlier — user creates a board on Pinterest, connects
  account, we pull pins from that specific board.

  Pros: user-curated quality, no scraping.
  Cons: waiting on Pinterest approval.

  My recommendation

  Ship #2 (multi-image upload) right now. It's honestly the best UX — same
  result as everything else without the friction. When Pinterest approves your
  app, we bolt on #3 as an alternative flow for people who prefer curating on
  Pinterest itself.

  Skip #1 unless you specifically want the "browse Pinterest from our app" feel.
   The paste-URLs UX is clunkier than just uploading files.

  Want me to build #2 now? Would take ~15 minutes: multi-upload dropzone in
  Product Studio, images become NB Pro style refs, same "don't copy content,
  only mood" hint. Say go.

⏺ Background command "npx tsc --noEmit 2&gt;&amp;1 | head -10; git add -A &amp;&amp; git commit -m "product studio: multi-image inspo (2-6 refs = mood-only mode; 1 ref stays strict copy)

Style refs UI now accepts up to 6 images. Server routes them:
- 1 ref → existing strict 'recreate this exact layout, swap in my product' mode
- 2+ refs → mood-only mode: NB Pro absorbs lighting/palette/composition energy but is explicitly told not to copy any products, brands, packaging, or people shown in the references

Users drop screenshots they saved (from Pinterest, Instagram, etc.) — hand-curated inspo, no scraping, no contamination.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 &lt;noreply@anthropic.com&gt;" &amp;&amp; git push &amp;&amp; vercel deploy --prod --yes 2&gt;&amp;1 | grep -iE "ready" | tail -1" completed (exit code 0)

⏺ You were right — the upload existed. But it was single-image "recreate this
  layout exactly" mode. Just extended it:

  Style refs now go 1 → 6 images, with two modes:

  - 1 image: same as before — strict copy of that ad's layout, swapping in your
  product.
  - 2 to 6 images: mood-only inspo mode — NB absorbs lighting, palette,
  composition energy from the whole batch, but is explicitly told NOT to copy
  any products, packaging, logos, or people in them. Your product's design is
  locked to its own reference photos.

  UX:
  - Click the Inspo tile → multi-select or drag+drop up to 6 files at once
  - Each thumbnail has an × to remove
  - Little counter tells you how many slots are left
  - Hint text under the composer switches between "strict mode" (1 ref) and
  "mood mode" (2+ refs)

  So the flow for your JAMU case: browse Pinterest normally → right-click 3-6
  pins you like → Save Image As → drag them all into the Inspo tile in one drop
  → shoot. Your product's label survives because NB is instructed to ignore any
  products in the mood refs and preserve only what's in the product-reference
  slot.

⏺ Background command "vercel deploy --prod --yes 2&gt;&amp;1 | grep -iE "ready" | tail -1" completed (exit code 0)

⏺ Deployed. Three real bugs behind what you saw:

  1. Scene ignored in most shots. Sonnet's concept generator was writing shot
  ideas like "moss pool", "black studio", "terracotta wall" — it never received
  the picked scene, so it invented locations. Every one of those concepts then
  anchored NB Pro to the wrong backdrop.

  Fix: the Sonnet concept call now carries a LOCATION LOCK block with the scene
  name + full scene prompt. Every generated concept is required to stay in that
  specific place. On top of that, every final render prompt gets a mandatory
  scene-lock clause referencing the anchor image.

  2. Product design drifting. The JAMU label was subtly redesigned in a couple
  of shots — no strict integrity clause in the render prompt was forcing
  pixel-fidelity to the reference.

  Fix: every render prompt now appends a HERO PRODUCT INTEGRITY clause:
  packaging/label/wordmark/illustration/colours/proportions must match the
  reference exactly. If the product doesn't fit the composition, adjust the
  composition — not the product.

  3. Phantom characters. You picked 2, sometimes a third appeared.

  Fix: a CAST LOCK clause on every render prompt explicitly states the exact
  count of people (or "product only") and forbids phantom bodies, silhouettes,
  or crowd members that aren't in the identity references.

  Try that same JAMU hilltop shoot again with 4 shots — you should get 4
  different framings all clearly at Hilltop Sky Horizon, JAMU can label intact,
  exactly 2 people.

⏺ Background command "npx tsc --noEmit 2&gt;&amp;1 | head -5; git add -A &amp;&amp; git commit -m "product studio: ban duotone/monochrome/filter concepts + product-colour-immunity clause

The 'Railing Shadow Duotone Graphic' shot came back with the JAMU can label wiped — NB Pro applied the duotone filter to the whole image including the product, destroying its artwork.

Two fixes:
- Sonnet concept generator now banned from drafting duotone/monochrome/sepia/tinted/high-contrast/single-colour concepts. Graphic feel must come from composition/light/typography, never an image-wide colour filter.
- Every render prompt now includes a PRODUCT COLOUR IMMUNITY clause: even if the concept applies a filter to the environment, the product itself renders in original full colour from its reference photos.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 &lt;noreply@anthropic.com&gt;" &amp;&amp; git push &amp;&amp; vercel deploy --prod --yes 2&gt;&amp;1 | grep -iE "ready" | tail -1" completed (exit code 0)

⏺ Deployed. Root cause on that shot:

  "Duotone Graphic" — Sonnet wrote a concept explicitly asking for a duotone
  filter treatment. NB Pro applied the blue duotone to the whole image,
  INCLUDING the JAMU can, which stripped the label design. Our product-integrity
   clause said "don't redesign the label" — NB doesn't consider a filter to be a
   redesign.

  Two-layer fix:

  1. Sonnet is now banned from drafting duotone / monochrome / sepia / tinted / 
  single-colour concepts entirely. The graphic/editorial feel must come from
  composition, lighting, and typography — never an image-wide colour filter.
  That whole class of concept won't get to NB in the first place.
  2. Every render prompt now includes a PRODUCT COLOUR IMMUNITY clause: even if
  the scene has a filter/tint applied, the product itself renders in its
  original full colour from the reference photos. The filter stops at the
  product.

  On the floating levitation shot — that one's technically correct (label
  intact, correct scene, product visible), just a bad composition (a can
  floating unrealistically in mid-air). That's a Sonnet aesthetic choice — the
  concept was literally "Floating Mid-Stair Levitation." If you want fewer
  surreal composited shots, the fix is to bias Sonnet toward realistic hands-on
  placements rather than banning the concept type. Say the word if you want that
   too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 &lt;noreply@anthropic.com&gt;" &amp;&amp; git push &amp;&amp; vercel deploy --prod --yes 2&gt;&amp;1 | grep -iE "ready" | tail -1" completed (exit code 0)

⏺ Deployed. Different root cause this time — the 3-attempts + backfill I added
  earlier only covered failed renders. What happened here is that Sonnet's
  concept generator returned only 2 valid concepts out of the requested 4 (its
  JSON output got truncated mid-array and the salvage parser only recovered 2
  objects). So the render pass only had 2 concepts to render — got 2 photos,
  backfill saw 0 missing renders, returned 2.

  Fix

  Concept short-fall guard: if the parsed concept count is less than requested,
  we pad the batch with variation-cue duplicates of the concepts we DO have ("— 
  variant 3" + "same setup shifted to a different moment", etc.). Guarantees the
   render pass always produces the requested count.

  maxDuration 180s → 300s so parallel renders + backfill can't hit the timeout
  ceiling on 4-shot batches.

  Combined with the earlier 3-inline-attempts + backfill, you should reliably
  get 4-out-of-4 now.

⏺ Reel Analyzer removed and deployed.

  On Workflows (ElevenLabs Flows / Arcads-style)

  Honest take: the concept is great, but the visual node-canvas execution is a 
  trap for a small team.

  What Flows genuinely solve:
  - Chain outputs (image → video → voiceover → composited final)
  - Rework any step without regenerating everything
  - Save + rerun the pipeline with new inputs
  - Sticky as hell — users invest in building the flow

  The trap:
  - Visual node canvas + edges + real-time state + step-level cache = 3–4 weeks
  of focused build minimum
  - ElevenLabs shipped that with a real team + designer
  - Most users don't build flows — they run pre-built ones. The canvas is
  impressive in a demo, rarely used in practice.
  - You already have Campaign Planner which is a form of workflow at higher
  abstraction

  My recommendation — a smarter middle path

  Phase 1 — "Recipes" (ships in a day)
  Not a canvas. A page like /recipes with 8–10 hard-coded pre-built workflows:
  - "Product ad from scratch" → product photo (Studio) → hero frame → 15s UGC
  video → captions
  - "Influencer launch" → create influencer → 4-shot lifestyle set → matching
  UGC ad
  - "1 photo → 5 outputs" → upload photo → variations at every aspect ratio + a
  10s clip
  - "Podcast ad" → 2 influencers → 6-shot dialogue → stitched final

  Each recipe = a simple form ("what's your product?") → runs endpoint chain
  server-side → user gets everything at once. Zero canvas. Cheap. Ships this
  week.

  This delivers 80% of what Flows delivers with 5% of the build cost.

  Phase 2 — visual Flow builder (much later, if data justifies it)
  Only build the canvas if:
  - Recipes are heavily used
  - Users are asking to modify recipes / build their own
  - You have designer bandwidth

  If you jump straight to the canvas, you'll spend a month on infra and end up
  with 5 users who actually build flows.

  What Arcads does

  Arcads' "flow" is basically a linear template chooser — pick a template, fill
  inputs, output. Not a node canvas. That's what I'd copy first.

  TL;DR

  Yes, ship it — but as Recipes first, not a Flow canvas. Say the word and I'll
  spec out 6 recipes and build the page.

⏺ Deployed. Podcast Ad lives at Video Studio → Podcast Ad tab
  (/generate/podcast-ad).

  What ships

  3-step flow:

  1. Setup — pick a product from your library (or type a new name), pick 2
  influencers (Host + Expert), optional brief + offer, pick 720p / 1080p.
  2. Script review — Sonnet drafts 6 shots of dialogue (host + expert lines)
  following the GRÜNS structure. Every line editable in place. Placeholder
  counts + word caps enforced by the prompt.
  3. Render — all 6 Seedance shots fire in parallel. Each card shows submitting
  → processing → completed with a playable MP4 inline. Page polls automatically
  every 6s.

  Production-grade prompts baked in

  lib/podcast-ad.ts encodes the full scaffolding from your reference guide:
  - Locked setting (premium studio, boucle sofa, gallery wall, RODE mics, no
  window)
  - Locked character wardrobe + skin realism (no smoothed AI look)
  - Pacing priority clause scales to word count (brisker on denser shots)
  - Audio-continues-under-cutaway rule
  - Lively reaction energy clause
  - Gesture logic tied to word meaning
  - Anatomy / RODE-text integrity in negative clauses
  - Shot 6 = handheld pull-back + rack-defocus + tilt down to product

  Costs

  ~1500 cr at 720p (~$36), ~3500 cr at 1080p. Total wall time: ~5 min once
  submitted (parallel).

  One thing not perfect (v1)

  Shot 6 wants shot 5's LAST frame as its start image for continuity. We don't
  yet extract frames from finished Seedance videos, so shot 6 uses the character
   references + product image and lets Seedance synthesise the seated
  composition. If shot 5 → shot 6 continuity is jarring in practice, next
  iteration: add a /api/video/last-frame extractor that pulls frame N from a
  completed MP4 and re-fires shot 6 chained to it. Say the word if you hit that
  and I'll wire it.

❯ whats the workflow of the format library's formats                            

⏺ Honest answer: the Format Library right now is mostly metadata + prompt hints,
   not a router to specialized pipelines. Let me walk through what actually
  happens:

  Today's workflow

  Where formats live
  - 28 formats registered in lib/campaign-formats.ts — each has key, label,
  tagline, category, pipeline, defaults, sonnetSpec

  Path 1 — Campaign Planner
  1. User writes a brief in /campaigns
  2. Sonnet picks format keys from the catalog when drafting the 20-30 shot list
  3. Each shot in the campaign carries its format_key
  4. Format is stored on the shot; the campaign detail table shows the label

  Path 2 — UGC Package Builder (the inline picker I just built)
  1. User clicks "📚 Pick a format from the Library"
  2. Modal shows 28 formats grouped by category
  3. User picks one → applyFormat(fmt) runs:
    - Duration snaps to nearest supported (5/10/15/20/30s)
    - Aspect maps (9:16 → portrait, etc.)
    - Director instructions field gets Format: {label}\n{sonnetSpec} prepended
  4. User still fills in the rest: product photo, character, benefits, CTA
  5. Standard UGC pipeline runs: Sonnet script → NB Pro hero frames → Seedance
  animate → final MP4

  What formats DON'T do yet (the real gap)

  The registry says a format has a pipeline like motion-broll or ugc-interview
  or ugc-couple — but the UGC Builder ignores that field. Every format runs
  through the standard ugc-video pipeline with different director instructions.
  So:

  - Aesthetic B-roll (should be no-dialogue product motion) → still renders as
  talking-head with the "no dialogue" hint in instructions. NB tries to comply
  but often fails.
  - Man-on-Street Interview (should have 2 people mid-street) → runs
  single-influencer talking-head with an interview hint.
  - Unboxing ASMR (should be hands-only) → still gets a face rendered.

  The Podcast Ad you just tested is the exception — it has its own dedicated
  page + 6-shot pipeline + specialized prompts. That's what "a format with a
  real workflow" looks like.

  What "proper format workflows" would mean

  For each format to have a real pipeline (like Podcast Ad does):
  - Motion formats (unboxing, ASMR, hyper-motion, crush test) → skip hero-frame
  + script steps, go straight to Seedance with product-first prompts
  - Two-person formats (interview, couple, roommate rec) → require 2
  influencers, use dual-character prompts
  - Photo formats (hero editorial, lifestyle in-scene, studio still) → route to
  Product Studio, not UGC pipeline
  - Solo talking-head formats (hot take, testimonial, gadget saved me, etc.) →
  current UGC pipeline is fine, they just need format-specific script prompts

  What I'd do (if you want to invest)

  Small win — add format-specific script scaffolds. Currently the script is
  generated the same way regardless of format. Adding per-format script system
  prompts (like the podcast ad has) would immediately make Hot Take vs
  Testimonial vs Gadget-Saved-Me produce visibly different outputs.

  Bigger win — route formats to their actual pipelines. Motion formats skip
  script entirely, photo formats go to Product Studio, two-person formats
  require 2 actors. This is a week of work but turns the Format Library from
  "prompt hints" into "actual format templates."

  Want me to build either? Or is the current inline picker enough for now and we
   move on?
